title: 2 Samuel 17:15–22
context: Hushai passes word through the priests Zadok and Abiathar. Their sons Jonathan and Ahimaaz, waiting at En Rogel, are spotted but hidden in a well at Bahurim by a woman who covers it with grain. They reach David, who crosses the Jordan with all his people by morning.

verses.text: Then Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, “Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel that way; and I have counseled this way.
verses.arminianNotes: Hushai tells Zadok and Abiathar both counsels. Arminian readers note the faithful cooperation of the priests and Hushai, each taking real risks to protect the king.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God using a network of faithful servants, arranged in advance in 15:27-36, to carry out his purpose of preserving David. Each servant plays a small part in a larger plan.

verses.text: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, ‘Don’t lodge tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means pass over, lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people who are with him.’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: Hushai urges David not to camp at the fords but to cross quickly. Arminian readers note that Hushai does not assume his counsel will be followed, and takes prudent steps in case Absalom changes his mind.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that trust in God’s providence does not exclude caution. Hushai acts urgently on the knowledge he has, an example of wise action alongside faith.

verses.text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying by En Rogel; and a female servant used to go and report to them, and they went and told King David; for they couldn’t risk being seen coming into the city.
verses.arminianNotes: Jonathan and Ahimaaz wait at En Rogel, receiving reports through a female servant. Arminian readers note the courage of ordinary people, including a servant girl, who take risks for the king.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that En Rogel lay on the border described in Joshua 18:16. They see God’s care for David working through hidden, humble channels.

verses.text: But a boy saw them, and told Absalom. Then they both went away quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his court; and they went down there.
verses.arminianNotes: A boy sees them and tells Absalom, and they flee to a house in Bahurim with a well. Arminian readers see how plans can be disrupted by unexpected events, requiring quick and courageous decisions.
verses.reformedNotes: Bahurim was where Shimei cursed David (16:5), yet here a household protects David’s messengers. Reformed readers note that God raises help even in places marked by hostility.

verses.text: The woman took and spread the covering over the well’s mouth, and spread out crushed grain on it; and nothing was known.
verses.arminianNotes: The woman covers the well and spreads grain over it. Arminian readers admire her quick thinking and courage, though they note that Christians have long discussed the ethics of deception in such cases.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers often compare her with Rahab hiding the spies (Joshua 2). They note that the narrative records her action without explicit approval, and that interpreters in both traditions differ on how to weigh such deception.

verses.text: Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house; and they said, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman said to them, “They have gone over the brook of water.” When they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: The woman tells Absalom’s servants the men have crossed the brook, and the searchers return empty-handed. Arminian readers note that her protective act saves lives at real risk to her own household.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s protection operating through this woman’s action. The searchers are turned back, and the message reaches David as God intends. The searchers’ failure is part of that care.

verses.text: After they had departed, they came up out of the well and went and told King David; and they said to David, “Arise and pass quickly over the water; for thus has Ahithophel counseled against you.”
verses.arminianNotes: The messengers climb out and urge David to cross the water quickly. Arminian readers note their faithful completion of a dangerous mission despite the close call.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that the warning reaches David in time. They see God’s purpose to preserve David moving forward through the obedience of these young men.

verses.text: Then David arose, and all the people who were with him, and they passed over the Jordan. By the morning light there lacked not one of them who had not gone over the Jordan.
verses.arminianNotes: David and all his people cross the Jordan by morning, with not one left behind. Arminian readers see the result of prompt obedience to a timely warning.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the completeness of the escape, with not one missing. They see God’s careful preservation of his anointed and those with him. The crossing marks a turning point in the conflict.
